title: Senior Treasury Manager - UK
description: <div> </div> <div><strong data-olk-copy-source="MessageBody">Location: London<br>Type: Full-time</strong></div> <div> </div> <div> <div data-olk-copy-source="MessageBody">BW ESS is seeking an experienced Senior Treasury Manager to take ownership of the Group's treasury activities across its international corporate entities, project SPVs and joint ventures.</div> <div data-olk-copy-source="MessageBody"> </div> <div>As BW ESS continues to grow, the complexity and importance of treasury is increasing materially. This role will bring together activities currently undertaken across different parts of the organisation, establish clear ownership and controls, and build a scalable treasury capability for the Group.</div> <div> </div> <div>This is a senior, hands-on role for someone who can both design the right treasury framework and make sure it operates effectively day to day. We are looking for candidates with real ownership experience in complex, multi-entity, multi-currency environments, ideally gained in energy, renewables, infrastructure, utilities or another project- and SPV-based business.</div> <div> </div> <div> <div><strong data-olk-copy-source="MessageBody">About BW ESS</strong></div> <div>BW ESS is a global energy storage owner-operator, moving with speed to develop, deliver and operate market-leading projects. The business is active in the UK, Australia, Italy, Germany, Spain, and Sweden. It has more than 540MWh of operating Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS), with ~12GWh under construction and a development pipeline of several gigawatts.</div> <div> </div> <div>Part of BW Group, BW ESS builds on decades of global infrastructure experience, takes a long-term view of projects and partnerships, and focuses on unlocking value throughout the energy storage asset lifecycle.</div> </div> </div> <div> </div> <div>To find out more, visit: <a href="https://bw-ess.com/">https://bw-ess.com/</a></div> <div> </div> <div> <div><strong data-olk-copy-source="MessageBody">The Role</strong></div> <div>Reporting to the Director of FP&A and Treasury, you will work closely with the CFO, Strategic Finance, Portfolio FP&A, Accounting, Tax, Investments, Legal and project teams, as well as BW Group and the Group's banking counterparties.</div> <div> </div> <div>You will be responsible for Group cash and liquidity management, credit support, FX and hedging operations, cash investment, banking and treasury facilities, treasury governance and treasury systems.</div> <div> </div> <div>Your objective is to replace fragmented activity with a coherent Group treasury capability: giving management reliable visibility of cash, liquidity and treasury risk, ensuring cash and credit resources are deployed efficiently, strengthening controls and banking infrastructure, and building processes and systems that scale with the business.</div> <div> </div> <div><strong>Key Responsibilities</strong></div> <ul> <li> <div>Cash management: own the consolidated Group cash position across corporate entities, project SPVs, joint ventures, accounts and currencies, including restricted and unrestricted cash, intercompany funding, equity contributions and distributions, and ensuring the right cash sits in the right entity, account and currency ahead of material payment obligations.</div> </li> <li> <div>Liquidity management: own the Group liquidity position and rolling forecast, consolidating inputs from Portfolio FP&A, Accounting, Investments, Strategic Finance and project teams, and providing forward-looking analysis of requirements, constraints, surpluses and funding needs across multiple currencies and jurisdictions.</div> </li> <li> <div>Credit support: own the portfolio of bank guarantees, parent-company guarantees, letters of credit and other contingent exposures, managing issuance, amendment, renewal and cancellation, and monitoring utilisation, expiries, fees, collateral and facility headroom.</div> </li> <li> <div>FX management: own the consolidated view of forecast and actual FX exposures across development, construction, operations and corporate activity, maintain the Group's FX framework, recommend hedging actions, and execute approved transactions within delegated authorities.</div> </li> <li> <div>Cash investment: manage surplus cash within approved policies and counterparty limits, optimising deposit arrangements, managing counterparty exposure and diversification, and negotiating terms to improve returns while preserving liquidity.</div> </li> <li> <div>Hedging operations: own the operational management of FX and interest-rate derivatives, including execution, confirmation, settlement, records of hedges and maturities, collateral and threshold monitoring, and treasury inputs into valuation, accounting and reporting.</div> </li> <li> <div>Banking and facilities: act as principal treasury relationship owner for cash-management and transaction banks, maintain the Group's banking architecture (accounts, mandates, signatories, access, KYC and documentation), own treasury-related facilities, and support complex funds flows for acquisitions, disposals, financings, refinancings and project financial close.</div> </li> <li> <div>Controls, policy and governance: own treasury policies, procedures, delegated authorities and the control framework, ensure transactions are authorised, documented, reconciled and auditable, monitor compliance with policy and counterparty limits, and report to senior management and governance forums.</div> </li> <li> <div>Systems and transformation: define the future treasury operating model, lead Treasury's contribution to the Group's ERP implementation, drive automation of cash visibility, forecasting, payments and bank-statement collection, and assess the role and timing of a dedicated Treasury Management System.</div> </li> </ul> <div><strong>Required Skills and Experience</strong></div> <ul> <li> <div>10+ years' relevant experience in corporate treasury, infrastructure, energy, banking or a closely related finance role.</div> </li> <li> <div>Demonstrable experience taking ownership of treasury activities in a complex, multi-entity, multi-currency organisation.</div> </li> <li> <div>Strong practical experience across cash and liquidity management, FX, banking, credit support and treasury controls.</div> </li> <li> <div>Experience managing senior relationships with banks and other financial counterparties.</div> </li> <li> <div>Strong understanding of treasury risk management, with the ability to translate financial exposures into practical recommendations and actions.</div> </li> <li> <div>Ability to operate effectively across multiple legal entities, jurisdictions, currencies and stakeholders.</div> </li> <li> <div>Strong judgement and the confidence to identify issues, challenge existing practice and recommend solutions to senior management.</div> </li> <li> <div>Comfortable working hands-on while building more scalable processes, controls and systems.</div> </li> <li> <div>Strong analytical capability and the ability to communicate complex treasury issues clearly and concisely.</div> </li> <li> <div>ACT, ACA, ACCA, CIMA or equivalent professional qualification preferred.</div> </li> </ul> <div><strong>Preferred Experience</strong></div> <ul> <li> <div>Energy, renewables, infrastructure, utilities or another project- and SPV-based business.</div> </li> <li> <div>Treasury within a business undergoing rapid international growth.</div> </li> <li> <div>Project finance, including restricted cash, reserve accounts and project-level funding structures.</div> </li> <li> <div>Bank guarantees, letters of credit, parent-company guarantees and other project credit support.</div> </li> <li> <div>FX and interest-rate derivatives, including ISDA-governed arrangements.</div> </li> <li> <div>ERP, Treasury Management System or wider finance-transformation implementation.</div> </li> <li> <div>Cash pooling, bank connectivity, automated payments and treasury reporting.</div> </li> <li> <div>Acquisition, disposal, refinancing and complex transaction funds flows.</div> </li> </ul> <div><strong>Why Join BW ESS?</strong></div> <div>This is an opportunity to join a fast-moving global energy storage owner-operator at a pivotal point in its growth, and to build the Group's treasury capability from a position of genuine ownership.</div> <div> </div> <div>If you are an experienced treasury professional who enjoys combining framework-building with hands-on delivery in an international, project-based business, we would like to hear from you.</div> <div> </div> <div><strong>Equal Opportunity</strong></div> <div>BW ESS is committed to building a high-performing, inclusive team and welcomes applications from candidates of all backgrounds</div> </div> <p> </p><div class="content-conclusion"><p><span data-olk-copy-source="MessageBody">Your personal information will be processed in accordance with our <a href="https://bw-ess.com/bw-ess-candidate-privacy-notice" target="_blank">Recruitment Privacy Notice</a>.</span></p></div> Find more English Speaking Jobs title: Product Manager, Homepage
description: <div class="content-intro"><h2><span data-sheets-root="1">About Wolt</span></h2> <p><span data-sheets-root="1">At Wolt, we create technology that brings joy, simplicity and earnings to the neighborhoods of the world. In 2014 we started with delivery of restaurant food. Now we’re building the delivery of (almost) everything and you’ll find us in over 500 cities in 30 countries around the world. In 2022 we joined forces with DoorDash and together we keep on dreaming big and expanding across the globe.<br><br>Working at Wolt isn’t always easy, but it’s definitely exciting. Here you’ll learn more, build more, and ship more than in most other companies. You’ll be challenged a lot, but also have a lot of fun on the way. So, if you’re a self-starter with drive and entrepreneurial spirit, this could be the ride of your life.</span></p></div><p>Join us in shaping the experience that millions of customers land on every time they open DoorDash, Wolt, or Deliveroo. As part of our Core Consumer organisation, our Homepage team owns one of the single biggest levers we have on what customers find and one of the hardest surfaces in the app to get right.</p> <p>Working at the intersection of ranking, personalisation, and AI/ML, you'll help decide what each customer sees and why, across three brands and dozens of markets. demonstrating curiosity, a willingness to learn, and sound judgment in applying AI responsibly to improve efficiency and impact. What you can expect as a Vanta’n: Industry-competitive salary and equity 100% covered medical, dental, and vision benefits with dependents coverage 16 weeks paid Parental Leave for all new parents Health & wellness stipend Remote workspace, internet, and mobile phone stipend Commuter benefits for team members who attend the office Pension matching 25 days of Annual Leave per year and unlimited sick time 8 company-paid holidays Virtual team building activities, lunch and learns, and other company-wide events! title: Member Experience Training & Quality Specialist - UK

A sharp eye for service detail and what separates a good experience from an exceptional one, drawn from service design and hospitality thinking rather than process alone. Excellent written and verbal communication, and the credibility to influence teams and leads who do not report to you. Willingness to travel regularly between clinic sites, and occasionally between markets. Experience supporting a multi-site clinic, hospitality, or retail rollout as it scales. Experience with digital learning tools, an LMS, or AI-enabled training and assessment. Confident with everyday workplace tools, including Microsoft Word, PowerPoint, Excel and Outlook, to build training materials, track audits and report findings. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. </strong></p> </div> </div> </div> </div></div><p></p> <p data-pm-slice="1 3 []">The New York Times is continuing to expand its video journalism, identifying compelling visual stories across the depth and breadth of our reporting. You will be expected to produce engaging stories through original reporting, on-the-ground filming, motion graphics and studio-based recordings.</p> <p>You must have deep experience reporting on stories from Europe, the Middle East and Africa, including managing teams in conflict zones, devising security plans and making risk assessments.</p> <p>This is a hybrid position based in London and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week.</p> <p><strong>Responsibilities will include:</strong></p> <ul> <li> <p>Drive innovative Reporter Video delivering on a range of formats.</p> </li> <li> <p>Build and strengthen relations with colleagues on the International Desk, including mentorship of reporters, photographers and fellow editors on the reporter video broadcast news.</p> </li> <li> <p>Proven track record managing direct reports.</p> </li> <li> <p>Demonstrated deep command of a variety of video sources, including wire services, UGC, archival footage, motion graphics, and original footage.</p> </li> </ul> <p><strong>Preferred Requirements:</strong></p> <ul> <li> <p>Excellent writing, editing and communication skills.</p> </li> <li> of a multidisciplinary team.</p> </li> <li> <p>Experience overseeing shoots and interviewing experts on camera.</p> </li> <li> <p>Familiar with digital storytelling formats.</p> </li> <li> <p>Understanding of mainstream and emerging social channels</p> </li> <li> <p>Flexibility to work extended hours.</p> </li> </ul> <p>REQ-020816</p> <p><strong>Additional Compensation and Benefits</strong><br><br>For roles in the U.S., dependent on your role, you may be eligible for variable pay, such as an annual bonus and restricted stock. Benefits may include medical, dental and vision benefits, Flexible Spending Accounts (F.S.A.s), a company-matching 401(k) plan, employee stock purchase plan, paid vacation, paid sick days, paid parental leave, tuition reimbursement and professional development programs.<br><br>For roles outside of the U.S., information on benefits will be provided during the interview process.</p><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>Candidate Use of GenAI Tools:</strong></p> <p>We’re excited to learn more about you and your experience. code review, CI and testing for models and platform code, so changes ship safely and repeatably</p> </li> </ul> <h2><strong>We’re excited about you because…</strong></h2> <ul> <li> <p>3+ years of experience in business intelligence engineering, analytics engineering, data engineering, or a similar code-first data role</p> </li> <li> <p>Strong Python and SQL skills, and hands-on experience using AI tools (LLMs, agentic workflows, AI-assisted development) to accelerate your own engineering work</p> </li> <li> <p>Hands-on experience building in a BI platform such as Looker (LookML) or Sigma, modelling and configuring it, not only building dashboards in it</p> </li> <li> <p>Experience with semantic or metrics layers (LookML, dbt or similar): defining metrics and dimensions, and keeping those definitions consistent as they are reused</p> </li> <li> <p>Experience running what you build in production: version control, code review, CI, debugging live issues and taking part in operational support</p> </li> <li> <p>Excellent communication skills, and comfortable self-organising in a fast-paced, distributed environment with both technical and non-technical teams</p> </li> </ul> <h2><strong>Nice to Have</strong></h2> <ul> <li> <p>Experience with modern data warehousing platforms (e.g., Snowflake, Databricks, Redshift) and ability to optimize performance</p> </li> <li> <p>Experience automating BI administration through platform APIs, or identity and access through Okta, SCIM or role-based access controls</p> </li> <li> <p>Experience supporting a BI stack across multiple brands, tenants or regions, or leading a BI platform migration</p> </li> </ul> <h2>Why Join Us?</h2> <p>At Deliveroo, you’ll do work that matters—solving real-world problems in a three-sided marketplace that’s constantly evolving. We’re food lovers, problem solvers, community builders and more, brought together by a shared drive to make things better. Working here you can expect to:</p> <p>🔧 <strong>Solve meaningful problems at real scale</strong> Work on a complex, always-on marketplace that impacts millions every day.</p> <p>🌱 <strong>See your impact, fast</strong> Ship, test and improve ideas quickly in a low-hierarchy, high-ownership environment.</p> <p>🧠 <strong>Grow through challenge and ownership</strong> Take on big, ambiguous problems and accelerate your career with strong support.</p> <p>🌎 <strong>A culture built for builders</strong> High standards, collaboration, flexible working and continuous learning.</p> <p>➡️ Want a deeper look at how we build? Explore our <a class="ng-star-inserted" href="https://careers.deliveroo.co.uk/interview-guide-for-engineers/" target="_blank">Engineering Interview Guide here</a> to help you feel confident at each stage.</p> <h3>Our Global Structure</h3> <p>Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Together, we’re unlocking new possibilities as one global team.</p><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>Diversity, Equity and Inclusion</strong><br><br>At Deliveroo, we know that a great workplace reflects the world around us and that true diversity and inclusion make us stronger, more creative, and better at what we do. With over 2,000 people across the UK, Europe, North America, Asia and Australia, the firm combines global insight with local understanding.</p> <p>The firm works across energy and resources, financial services, government and public sector, consumer products and retail, pharmaceuticals and life sciences, manufacturing, and technology, media and telecoms, with capabilities spanning strategy, transformation and operational excellence – all powered by advanced technology, data, AI and digital innovation.</p> <p>Clients value Baringa’s collaborative approach and the way its teams integrate seamlessly – all working with a shared understanding of what matters most. title: Senior Sales Manager - Issuing
description: Company Description We’re Checkout.com . You might not know our name, but companies like eBay, Spotify, Klarna, Uber, and Sony do, because we’re behind many of the digital experiences you use every day. We are where the world checks out, enabling over 10 billion transactions yearly for more than one billion global shoppers. Whether you want to book a holiday, order food, renew a subscription, or check out online, there’s a good chance our tech powers the payments behind the scenes. Our platform helps the most ambitious businesses deliver effortless digital experiences, at scale. If you want to do career-defining work, you’ve come to the right place. We move fast, think globally, and believe great teams are built by hiring exceptional people with conviction, curiosity, and the desire to make an impact. With 20 offices across six continents and London as our HQ, we’re shaping the future of fintech – and we’re just getting started. The Role Checkout.com are actively looking for an enthusiastic and talented Senior Sales Manager to join our Commercial Team in London to drive rapid growth for our revolutionary Card Issuing solution. We need a high-achieving individual to help global enterprises launch modern card programs—from virtual cards for travel intermediaries to physical cards for BNPL. If you are a driven and focused salesperson with a proven track record of selling cutting edge issuing solutions in a high-growth and competitive environment, this is the role for you. In return, on top of a tremendous working environment, we offer you an unrivalled uncapped recurring commissions plan. Reporting to the Director, the Senior Sales Manager will handle multiple sales cycles, always ensuring a high conversion rate and outperforming the sales targets. Along the way, you'll collaborate closely with various in-house talents across Technology and Business to position our capabilities, products, services and solutions effectively with prospects. The ideal candidate will need to be an independent, high-achieving individual, able to stand out in an entrepreneurial environment and outperform sales targets through personal drive. How You’ll Make an Impact Pipeline Growth: Identify the most promising clients and grow a healthy pipeline for card issuing across various verticals. Solution Selling: Sell our issuing products to travel intermediaries and fintech clients through outbound techniques. Consultative Expert: Help prospects evaluate Checkout.com, handling detailed questions about our product capabilities, serving as a consultant and industry expert. Proposal Management: Prepare thorough presentations and proposals that highlight the ROI of switching to a modern issuer. Full Cycle Orchestration: Lead the entire Sales process, acting as the main point of contact for clients and internal stakeholders. Collaboration: Partner with other Sales team members to share best practices, key business insights and industry trends Market Intelligence: Provide feedback on local trends including competitor insights, customer needs, sales, product and marketing information What We’re Looking For Experience: 5+ years of Sales experience, with at least 3 years specifically within Payments or Card Issuing. Network: A solid network of potential prospects and partners. AI & Productivity: Proficient in leveraging AI-powered sales tools to augment prospecting and analyze deal intelligence to accelerate the sales cycle. Technical Passion: Tech-savvy with a passion for how technology is transforming finance. Business Acumen: Solid understanding of financial factors, including interchange mechanics and card scheme products. Soft Skills: Exceptional communication and negotiation techniques, with the ability to navigate complex, multi-stakeholder deals. Tools: Knowledge of Salesforce and a highly organized approach to prioritizing shifting workloads. Additional Information Bring all of you to work We create the conditions for high performers to thrive, through real ownership, fewer blockers, and work that makes a difference from day one. Here, you’ll move fast, take on meaningful challenges, and be recognized for the impact you deliver. It’s a place where ambition gets met with opportunity, and where your growth is in your hands. We work as one team, and we back each other to succeed. So whatever your background or identity, if you’re ready to grow and make a difference, you’ll be right at home here. It’s important we set you up for success and make our process as accessible as possible. So let us know in your application, or tell your recruiter directly, if you need anything to make your experience or working environment more comfortable. Life at Checkout.com We understand that work is just one part of your life. Our hybrid working model offers flexibility, with three days per week in the office to support collaboration and connection. Curious about what it’s like to be part of our team? Visit our Careers Page to learn more about our culture, open roles, and what drives us. For a closer look at daily life at Checkout.com , follow us on LinkedIn and Instagram Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Strategic Customer Success Manager
description: A little about us incident.io is the AI software reliability platform trusted by engineering teams at Netflix, Etsy, and 2,000+ companies who can't afford downtime. The stakes are real, the talent is insane, and somehow it's a genuinely lovely place to work. We all pull our weight, go the extra mile, and put in the bit of magic most companies don't have time for, all while having fun and never taking ourselves too seriously. We've raised $100+ million from Index Ventures, Insight Partners, and Point Nine, and we're growing fast. There's never been a better time to join. The role in one line As our first EMEA Strategic Customer Success Manager, you’ll help define what strategic success looks like at incident.io , and become the trusted partner who makes us core to how the biggest enterprises run reliability. What that looks like day to day You’ll work with a small number of our largest, most complex and highest-value customers. These are established, often global and regulated enterprises, where buying decisions take time, many business units are involved, and incident management is part of a wider move away from legacy tools and processes. You’ll be their strategic partner across the full lifecycle, from early involvement in the deal with Sales through to adoption and expansion, and from the on-call engineer to the CIO and CTO. You’ll help land strategic logos with focused first contracts, then build the business case and success plan that turns them into larger deals. From there you’ll expand across the enterprise, mapping the organisation, finding champions and repeating proven wins across business units and regions. You’ll run Executive Business Reviews and connect our leadership with theirs, tying what we do to what matters to their business: operational resilience, regulatory risk, the cost of downtime, tool consolidation, MTTR reduction and incident process maturity. You’ll lead onboarding and migrations in organisations that move carefully, moving them off legacy tools and ITSM-led processes and making the change stick, including deeper adoption across Response, On-call, Status Pages and our AI capabilities. You’ll spot and reduce business, operational and reputational risk before it becomes visible, and bring Sales, Solutions Engineering, Product, Marketing and Support together around shared goals for each account, including expansion and renewals. You’ll also work directly with Product and Engineering on the roadmap and design partnerships. As the first EMEA Strategic CSM and third on the team overall, you’ll help define our strategic CS playbook, support high-stakes deals and help develop your peers as the segment grows. Who you are You have significant experience in Customer Success, Account Management or Technical Account Management, managing strategic or Fortune 500-scale accounts in enterprise SaaS. Traditional enterprises like financial services, insurance, pharma, retail or private equity are ideal. Developer tooling, observability or incident management is a plus. You’ve driven adoption, retention and expansion in large, complex accounts with many stakeholders, and you have results you can point to. You know how to land small and grow large, turning a pilot or single business unit into a multi-BU footprint over a long sales cycle. Building a business case doesn’t faze you, nor does navigating procurement, security, legal and change management in slow-moving organisations. You’re confident with senior technical executives, running EBRs and strategic planning sessions, and just as comfortable going deep with SREs and platform engineers. You’re technically fluent in modern engineering organisations, on-call, incident response, SRE practices and the observability and DevOps ecosystem, and you can translate it for business stakeholders. You have strong commercial judgement, partner well with Sales on renewals and expansion, and get ahead of customer challenges rather than reacting to them. You’re autonomous and comfortable with ambiguity. You’re excited to define the role, not just step into it. Supporting you We work hard and we think life outside work matters just as much. Our benefits pack is built to support both. Private medical insurance. Seriously good cover - we want you and the people you love to be looked after. Competitive annual leave. Showing up at your best requires switching off, and we make sure you have time to do that. First Friday of every month off. Yes, seriously. Enhanced pension. We put real money in, because future-you deserves better than an afterthought. Meaningful equity. We’re rapidly scaling, and everyone who helps shape the outcome should share in it. Unlimited AI spend. For everyone, not just engineers. We’re all-in on AI across the company, and we expect you to be too. Generous parental leave. The early days with a new baby matter more than anything we’re doing here, and we want you to be present for them. Two budgets that have your back. £1000 to invest in your setup, £500 a year to invest in yourself. Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Director of Quality
description: About LILT AI is changing how the world communicates — and LILT is leading that transformation. We're on a mission to make the world's information accessible to everyone , regardless of the language they speak. We use cutting-edge AI, machine translation, and human-in-the-loop expertise to translate content faster, more accurately, and more cost-effectively without compromising on brand, voice, or quality. At LILT, we empower our teammates with leading tools, global collaboration, and growth opportunities to do their best work. Our company virtues— Work together, win together; Find a way or make one; Dance in the customer's shoes; Quicker than they expect; Quality is Job 1 —guide everything we do. We are trusted by Intel Corporation , Canva , the United States Department of Defense , the United States Air Force , ASICS , and hundreds of global Enterprises. Backed by Sequoia, Intel Capital, and Redpoint, we’re building a category-defining company in a $50B+ global translation market being redefined by AI. Location: Remote or hybrid, EMEA or US Eastern time zone Team: Production, Quality Reports to: VP Production Direct reports: Quality Manager (AMER, customer staffing) and 2 Quality Coordinators About the role As Director of Quality, you will own LILT's quality system end to end: standards, audit, compliance, procedures, continuous improvement, and the roadmap and operation of our Quality Agents . You'll help move Quality from a primarily reactive, execution-led function to a proactive, data-driven partner for customers and internal teams, with quality designed into our AI-native workflows. You'll be the person who can run a customer audit while simultaneously shipping an improved agent evaluation. As the single Quality partner for Customer Success, Production, Research and Product, you'll turn customer requirements into measurable acceptance criteria, effective controls and better models and workflows. You'll advise customers on the right quality, cost and speed mix, including where automated, agent-verified and human-verified workflows are appropriate, with stronger assurance for high-risk and regulated content. We're looking for a hands-on Quality SME and operator with real depth in both worlds: experience designing and building AI agents and improving LLM output, and a solid grounding in traditional quality management. You'll bring senior expertise in data, AI, customer advisory and process, and make sure quality work prevents recurrence rather than stopping at rework or ticket closure. What you'll do Quality Agent leadership Evaluate, design and build reliable Quality Agents with well-defined tools and clear, structured instructions. Use orchestration patterns to evolve from a single agent to multi-agent systems. Define evaluation criteria, test sets and success metrics for agent performance, and run agents in production with clear monitoring and escalation paths. Drive adoption across teams and show measurable reductions in manual quality effort. Research and Product partnership Work closely with Research and Product on ADQ, LLM model improvements, AI Review, AI QA, and new and emerging AI workflows. Turn quality findings into product requirements, evaluation criteria and continuous feedback loops that improve model and workflow output. Act as the voice of quality in roadmap discussions, and help decide where human review, AI review or both are needed. Audit, compliance and procedure Own LILT's approach to internal and external audits, including ISO certification (e.g. ISO 17100, ISO 18587, ISO 9001) and customer audits. Plan and run periodic internal audits, manage evidence collection, and track corrective and preventive actions to closure. Standardise and maintain SOPs, workflows and quality documentation, and keep them current as AI workflows change how we work. Make sure quality processes meet customer, contractual and regulatory requirements. Customer advisory Partner with Customer Success and Delivery to define proactive quality programmes, success metrics and governance for strategic accounts, including AI-forward enterprise and life science / regulatory programmes. Translate customer quality requirements into clear pre-delivery acceptance criteria, validation methods and risk-appropriate controls. Advise customers on the right quality, cost and speed mix and where automated, agent-verified, human-verified or combined workflows are appropriate. Represent LILT's quality function as a credible subject-matter authority in customer business reviews, audits and escalations, using quality data and metrics to demonstrate fitness for purpose. Continuous improvement Lead structured CI across the Commercial business: root cause analysis, corrective and preventive actions, KPI reviews and retrospectives. Own a proactive quality metrics framework that makes errors, PQs, rework and trends visible, and use it to prioritise improvements and demonstrate outcomes. Strengthen quality controls across review, delivery and follow-through, including mandatory account-specific checks, intervention on critical findings and clear escalation ownership. Partner with Product and Engineering to automate checks and escalation, and verify that corrective actions prevent recurrence rather than ending at rework or ticket closure. Expert Operations partnership Partner with Expert Supply and Ops to embed processes, guidance and quality feedback that maintain a high-quality pipeline of experts. Use quality findings and recurring failure patterns to improve expert qualification, guidance and ongoing quality management. Team leadership Lead and develop the Quality team, including the customer-facing Quality Manager and Quality Coordinators. Establish the team's operating cadence and evolve how the team works as Quality Agents reduce manual coordination work. Oversee embedded Quality Manager staffing sold as a service to customers, ensuring the role owns the specific quality programmes and initiatives those customers pay for. Develop playbooks for AI-driven quality management and keep staffing-as-a-service delivery aligned with LILT's quality standards. What you'll bring Must have Agent design and build: demonstrable, hands-on experience designing, building and running LLM-based agents in production. Please be ready to walk us through agents you have built. Data-driven quality management: scripting or data skills (e.g. Python, SQL), with experience turning quality data into actionable metrics, preventive controls and measurable improvements. LLM model improvement: proven experience improving LLM output quality. Significant experience running quality systems , including leading audits (internal and external), compliance programmes, and writing and maintaining processes and procedures. Quality certifications such as Six Sigma are a plus. Experience leading structured CI (RCA, CAPA, KPI reviews). Experience managing and developing people. Customer advisory and cross-functional partnership: a clear communicator who can translate customer quality requirements into acceptance criteria and governance, advise on quality, cost and speed trade-offs, and work credibly with customers, executives and technical teams. Nice to have Background in localisation, translation or language services. Experience in customer-facing quality roles for enterprise accounts. Research and Product collaboration: a track record of working with research scientists and product managers to turn quality insight into product requirements and shipped improvements. Our Story Our founders, Spence and John met at Google working on Google Translate. As researchers at Stanford and Berkeley, they both worked on language technology to make information accessible to everyone. While together at Google, they were amazed to learn that Google Translate wasn’t used for enterprise products and services inside the company.The quality just wasn’t there. So they set out to build something better. LILT was born. LILT has been a machine learning company since its founding in 2015. At the time, machine translation didn’t meet the quality standard for enterprise translations, so LILT assembled a cutting-edge research team tasked with closing that gap. While meeting customer demand for translation services, LILT has prioritized investments in Large Language Models, human-in-the-loop systems, and now agentic AI. With AI innovation accelerating and enterprise demand growing, the next phase of LILT’s journey is just beginning. Our Tech What sets our platform apart: Brand-aware AI that learns your voice, tone, and terminology to ensure every translation is accurate and consistent Agentic AI workflows that automate the entire translation process from content ingestion to quality review to publishing 100+ native integrations with systems like Adobe Experience Manager, Webflow, Salesforce, GitHub, and Google Drive to simplify content translation Human-in-the-loop reviews via our global network of professional linguists, for high-impact content that requires expert review LILT in the News Featured in The Software Report’s Top 100 Software Companies! LILT makes it onto the Inc. 5000 List . LILT’s continues to be an intellectual powerhouse, holding numerous patents that help power the most efficient and sophisticated AI and language models in the industry. title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer, ADAS
description: Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve. We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that. Here’s what this particular role covers. 🛠️ About our ADAS Team Wayve's ADAS engineering teams build the perception and intelligence that power driver assistance in real-world driving. We work end-to-end, from creating high-quality training data, to developing and evaluating CV/3D perception models, to iterating quickly based on performance gaps. The team mixes "online" (on-car, latency/compute constrained) and "offline" (heavier, large-scale data generation) work, with a strong focus on measurable impact and shipping. 🧠 Your day-to-day Train, debug, and improve computer vision and 3D perception models, iterating based on clear evaluation signals Work across the full ML lifecycle: data, training, evaluation, and iteration Partner with the team to decide what to tackle next, based on where the system is underperforming Build scalable data pipelines, including auto-labelling and pseudo-labelling, to accelerate model development 🧩 What you'll be working on: Core ADAS perception capabilities such as detection, classification, and instance segmentation, spanning lanes, objects, traffic signs, and traffic lights End-to-end approaches that let the model act on the world directly, rather than relying on a chain of hand-coded intermediate steps (lane assist without ever explicitly detecting lane lines is the kind of outcome we're after) Online perception that runs fast in-car as part of our production stack Offline perception work using additional inputs not viable for on-road production, including extra sensors like lidar, future frames, maps, and extra compute, to improve data quality and coverage at scale Building the "data flywheel": using offline models and 3D tracking/reconstruction to auto-generate labels and accelerate iteration across perception tasks 👤 You should apply if: Built and shipped CV-focused deep learning systems, with strong applied ML engineering rather than research-only work Experience with 3D perception concepts or pipelines, such as LiDAR, multi-view geometry, tracking, or 3D reconstruction Comfortable owning work end-to-end, including evaluation and large-scale dataset generation Enjoy pragmatic problem-solving under real product constraints Excited to improve real-world driving performance through better perception Automotive domain experience is a bonus, but not a blocker if your perception background comes from elsewhere 🌱 Not ticking every box? That's totally okay! If you're passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don't meet every requirement. More about Wayve: 🚗 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines. Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve's mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility. How we work 💻 — Locations & Flexible Working: Our main hubs are in London, Sunnyvale, Yokohama, Herzliya, Vancouver and Leonberg. We operate a hybrid working model that combines in-person collaboration in our dedicated office spaces with focused time working remotely. This gives our teams the connection and energy of working together, alongside the flexibility to do their best work in a way that fits their lives. 📋 The Interview Process: Our process is clear and respectful of your time: Initial call / recruiter screen (30 mins) Competency interviews (programming and system design; 2 hours) Deep-dive technical interviews (Hiring manager/Domain Interview; 1 hour) Final interview : mission & values alignment (1 hour) We'll always explain the format and work around your availability. What's in it for you (Location dependent): 💰 Salaries benchmarked against the market annually 📈 Meaningful equity, sharing in the ownership and long term success of Wayve ✈️ Relocation support and visa sponsorship where applicable ✅ Hybrid working, core hours and the chance to work hands on in vehicle workshops and labs 📚 Learning and development budgets with support for training, conferences and growth 🩺 Comprehensive benefits including health insurance, dental, enhanced maternity and paternity leave, retirement or pension where applicable, access to therapists, wellbeing partner discounts and more A quick, honest note before you apply. Wayve is not a mature, fully-structured place with the playbook already written. Much of how we work is still being written, and if you join, you’ll help write it. That suits people who want real ownership more than people who need a settled structure from day one. If that sounds like the kind of problem you want to spend your time on, we’d really like to hear from you. At Wayve we're committed to creating a diverse, fair and respectful culture that is inclusive of everyone based on their unique skills and perspectives, and regardless of sex, race, religion or belief, ethnic or national origin, disability, age, citizenship, marital, domestic or civil partnership status, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, pregnancy or related condition (including breastfeeding) or any other basis as protected by applicable law. For more information visit Careers at Wayve. To learn more about what drives us, visit Values at Wayve DISCLAIMER: We will not ask about marriage or pregnancy, care responsibilities or disabilities in any of our job adverts or interviews. However, we do look to capture information about care responsibilities, and disabilities among other diversity information as part of an optional DEI Monitoring form to help us identify areas of improvement in our hiring process and ensure that the process is inclusive and non-discriminatory. title: Senior People Partner
description: Senior People Partner Cloudscaler | London | People Team | Reports to the Chief People Officer | £55,000–£75,000 Someone has to own the People initiative that doesn’t fit neatly into anyone’s week and the case nobody else should be handling. That someone is you — not as an escalation point, but as the person who runs the day-to-day of this function. THE MOMENT Cloudscaler is 130 people today. We’ll be 170 by the end of this year, and roughly double again in 2027. The People function is being built in real time alongside that growth, rather than inherited from someone who left years ago. You’ll be the first hire into the People team. For roughly your first year you’ll be the only People professional alongside the CPO, which means running the whole day-to-day of the function: the hardest casework and initiatives, and the operational core that keeps everything moving. A People Partner is planned to join later in 2027, and at that point the operational administration moves to them. This is also a role built with room to grow. As the team expands beyond that second hire, we expect this role to take on day-to-day operational leadership of the People Partner practice, but that isn’t the shape of it on day one. WHAT MAKES THIS DIFFERENT In most People teams, the senior generalist is just a People Partner with a harder case queue. Here, the difference is ownership, not just difficulty. Complex casework: Rather than simply handling harder cases, you’ll own the most complex cases end to end, with no hand back. People initiatives: Rather than contributing to initiatives someone else drives, you’ll own them from design through to embedding. Decision-making: Rather than escalating ambiguity upward, you’ll make the sensible call and document your reasoning. CPO partnership: Rather than acting in a support role to the CPO, you’ll be an operational partner they can confidently delegate to. To be clear about the level: The CPO still designs the People strategy and the systems architecture. You own how it runs day to day, and you’re trusted to run a whole initiative, not just a case. That is a different job to People Partner, not a bigger version of the same one. THE ROLE You’ll sit in the People team reporting to the Chief People Officer. Three strands make up the job: Casework: The employee relations situations with the most complexity or sensitivity land with you, start to finish. Initiatives: When the CPO needs a piece of work owned (a policy rollout, a wellbeing programme, a piece of the reward or benefits agenda), you take it from design through to something that runs. Operations: Until the People Partner joins, you’ll own payroll and benefits administration, onboarding, screening and security clearances, and keeping Rippling accurate. When the People Partner joins, they’ll report to the CPO. You won’t manage them formally, but you’ll lead their handover, you’ll be the person they come to first, and your judgement will set the standard for how this function operates day to day. WHERE THE ROLE STARTS AND STOPS New roles get vague, so here is the boundary as we see it today. Yours The most complex and sensitive employee relations casework, end to end. Full ownership of People initiatives, from design to embedding. Acting as the CPO’s operational partner on ambiguous or cross-cutting problems. Until the People Partner joins (planned for later in 2027): Payroll and benefits administration, including the monthly payroll cycle in Rippling and Mintago. Pre-onboarding, onboarding and probation. Background screening in Zinc. Security clearance coordination. Rippling data quality, workflows and reporting. Our working groups and committees. Once the People Partner joins: A structured handover of the operational core. Day-to-day guidance for the People Partner. Shared Ashby, which Talent Acquisition owns. You’ll work in it from offer through to start date on every hire until the People Partner joins, and on senior hires after that. Mentoring and supporting the People Partner on their casework and initiatives, once they join. Not yours Recruitment delivery, which sits with Talent Acquisition. The design of the People strategy, the operating model and the systems architecture, which sit with the CPO. Formal line management of the People Partner, who will report to the CPO. THE STACK Rippling: Our single source of truth. Until the People Partner joins you’ll run it day to day, including the monthly payroll cycle, data quality and workflows, and you’ll use its reporting at a level that supports whole initiatives. Zinc: Background screening. You’ll run checks for every new joiner until the People Partner joins, and stay close to the senior and sensitive hires after that. Ashby: Owned by Talent Acquisition. You’ll work in it from offer through to start date on the hires you’re responsible for. Claude: A daily tool here. You’ll use it for casework preparation, drafting policy and communications, and pulling together the analysis behind an initiative. Mintago: Our employee benefits and financial wellbeing platform (pensions, salary sacrifice and financial advice). You’ll administer it and keep enrolment accurate until the People Partner takes it on. WHAT YOU’LL DO Own the hardest casework. You’ll run our most complex and sensitive employee relations cases end to end, with the CPO there to sense-check rather than take over. Own initiatives, not tasks. You’ll take a People initiative from a rough brief to something that’s running and embedded, rather than handing it back once the interesting part is done. Run the operational core. Until the People Partner joins, you’ll own the monthly payroll cycle in Rippling, benefits administration including Mintago, onboarding, background screening and security clearances. Accurate, on time, and documented as you go. Hand it over well. When the People Partner arrives, you’ll give them a working system and a clear handover, then stay the person they come to first and the judgement others in the function measure themselves against. Partner with senior leaders. You’ll be credible with leaders on the most difficult conversations: complex change, capability, and situations without a clean playbook. Use AI properly. You’ll use Claude daily to take time out of your own week, checking anything that touches a decision about a person and owning the outcome. Improve what you find. You’ll spot the gaps in policy, process or practice before anyone else does, and bring the CPO a considered view on the fix, not just the problem. WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE AT 12 MONTHS You’re running the most complex ER cases with confidence, and the CPO isn’t being pulled into them. At least one or two People initiatives have gone from a rough brief to something genuinely embedded, owned by you. Payroll, benefits, onboarding and clearances run accurately and on time, and every process is documented well enough to hand over. You’ve helped shape the People Partner hire, so the handover is ready when they land. Senior leaders treat you as a credible operational partner, not an escalation point. You’ve made and documented sensible calls in genuinely ambiguous situations, and they’ve held up. The CPO can hand you an ambiguous problem and trust it gets shaped properly. WHO WE’RE LOOKING FOR Deep employee relations experience. You’ve run complex disciplinaries, grievances and change situations yourself, and you know exactly when to escalate and when not to. CIPD qualification, or solid progress towards it, is welcome. A track record of owning initiatives. You can point to work you took from a brief to something that actually ran, not just a project you contributed to. Hands-on with the operational detail. You’ve owned or closely supported a payroll cycle, benefits administration and onboarding, and you’re comfortable being accountable for their accuracy while also carrying the senior work. Credible with senior leaders. You can hold your own in a difficult conversation with someone under real pressure and be listened to. Comfortable operating near-autonomously. You don’t need a playbook for everything. You make a sensible call, write it down, and check it with the CPO afterwards. Ready to grow into people leadership. You won’t formally manage anyone at the start, but you’ll induct and guide the People Partner when they join, and you should want to lead a team as the structure catches up. Discreet and organised at volume. Complex casework and live initiatives, often at the same time. You’ll need a system, and it can’t be your memory. THE HONEST PART This role sits in an odd space for now: senior in scope and judgement, without a team underneath it yet. Until the People Partner joins later in 2027, you’ll also be the whole operational team, so a payroll deadline and a complex grievance can land in the same week. That eases as the function grows, but it means the authority you carry day to day has to come from the quality of your work, not a job title. You are not designing the People strategy or the systems architecture. The CPO does that. What you get instead is real ownership of the hardest cases and the initiatives that matter, a close working relationship with the CPO, and a genuine path toward leading the People Partner practice as it grows. This probably isn’t for you if you want a formal team from day one, or if you’d rather leave payroll and onboarding to someone else. It probably is for you if you want to prove you can run this function well enough, top to bottom, that a team gets built around you. If that sounds like the challenge you’ve been looking for, let’s talk. title: Senior Manager, Credit Risk
description: About Airwallex Airwallex is the AI-native financial operating system for a real-time, intelligent economy. More than 675,000 businesses, including McLaren Racing, Qantas, SHEIN, and TikTok, use us, directly or through our platform partners, to run their financial operations or build and monetize financial products of their own. We started in Melbourne in 2015 to build the infrastructure global commerce runs on. We're the regulated backbone behind global payments: not by accident, but by design. A decade plus, 85+ licenses, and a financial infrastructure spanning North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific. We're co-headquartered in San Francisco and Singapore, with more than 2,300 people across 27 offices. We hire builders with founder-level energy, people who move fast with good judgment, dig in with real curiosity, and make calls from first principles rather than waiting to be told what to do. Read our operating principles to see it in full. About the team The Credit Risk team is part of Airwallex’s Second Line of Defence and helps the company grow responsibly as a global financial platform. We work at the intersection of credit, FX, and counterparty risk, partnering closely with Product, Sales, Operations, Treasury, Finance, Engineering, Compliance, and Legal to enable commercial growth while protecting Airwallex from financial loss and excessive risk exposure. This is a team for analytical, commercially minded risk leaders who are energized by building scalable frameworks and practical controls across a fast-moving, multi-currency global network. What you'll do As a Senior Manager, Credit Risk, you will lead Airwallex's global second-line oversight of credit, FX, and counterparty risk. You will set the risk guardrails that allow the business to grow safely across merchant acquiring, charge cards, FX, treasury, settlement, and banking-partner activities. Reporting to the Senior Director, Financial Risk, you will own the global framework, risk appetite, limits, governance, and portfolio oversight for these risk areas. You will provide independent challenge to first-line decisions and act as a trusted advisor to senior leaders across the business. This role is based in London. Responsibilities Credit risk framework and risk appetite: Define, implement, and continuously enhance the global second-line credit risk framework, including policies, risk appetite thresholds, limits, escalation protocols, and governance standards across Airwallex’s products and legal entities. Credit portfolio oversight: Oversee credit exposures across merchant acquiring, charge cards, B2B and commercial activities, FX pre-funding, treasury-related exposures, settlement flows, and other relevant products. Underwriting and limit governance: Review and challenge first-line underwriting strategies, customer and merchant risk policies, credit assessments, limit-setting methodologies, and exception processes. Act as a senior escalation point for complex or high-value credit decisions. FX risk oversight: Establish and monitor appropriate second-line guardrails for FX exposures arising from pre-funding, settlement, customer activity, treasury flows, and other multi-currency activities. Challenge controls, limits, escalation triggers, and risk reporting to ensure exposures remain within approved tolerances. Counterparty risk management: Set and oversee counterparty risk standards for banking partners, payment partners, merchants, customers, and other material counterparties. Establish appropriate exposure limits, concentration thresholds, monitoring requirements, and escalation processes. Portfolio monitoring and early warning indicators: Lead proactive monitoring of credit, FX, and counterparty portfolios, including exposure, concentration, delinquency, default, chargeback, loss, settlement, liquidity-of-counterparty, and other relevant risk indicators. Identify emerging trends and escalate material issues before they become systemic. Loss mitigation and remediation: Review and challenge first-line monitoring, collections, collateral, prefunding, reserves, chargeback, and other mitigation strategies. Ensure deteriorating counterparties, customers, merchants, or exposures are identified and addressed promptly. New products and market expansion: Partner with Product, Engineering, Commercial, Treasury, Finance, and Operations to assess and challenge the risk design of new products, features, markets, currencies, and partner arrangements before launch. Risk approvals and governance: Lead or support risk committee decisions, material risk approvals, limit exceptions, breach assessments, and remediation plans. Ensure decisions are documented clearly and aligned with approved risk appetite. Regulatory and partner engagement: Represent Credit Risk during regulatory examinations, internal and external audits, and reviews with banking and strategic partners. Prepare clear, decision-useful materials for senior management, risk committees, and the Board where appropriate. Who you are We're looking for people who meet the minimum requirements for this role. The preferred qualifications are great to have, but are not mandatory. Minimum qualifications 10–15 years of progressively senior experience across credit risk, counterparty risk, FX risk, treasury risk, or related financial risk disciplines within banking, payments, fintech, or another highly regulated financial services environment. Deep experience designing, implementing, and governing second-line credit risk frameworks in a complex, multi-jurisdictional organization. Strong understanding of credit risk identification, measurement, underwriting, limit management, monitoring, mitigation, provisioning, loss recognition, and capital implications. Demonstrated experience managing risk across multiple product lines, such as merchant acquiring, commercial or charge cards, B2B lending, payment processing, FX, treasury, settlement, or banking-partner activities. Practical experience overseeing FX and counterparty risk, including exposure measurement, concentration risk, limits, settlement risk, prefunding, collateral or other mitigants, and escalation governance. Proven ability to challenge first-line decisions and communicate clear risk positions to senior executives, commercial leaders, product and operations teams, banking partners, auditors, and regulators. Preferred qualifications Advanced degree such as an MBA or Master's in Finance, Economics, Risk Management, or a related field. Professional certification such as FRM, PRM, CFA, or an equivalent qualification. Experience with automated decisioning engines, credit scoring models, portfolio analytics, or alternative data used in underwriting and monitoring. Familiarity with IFRS 9, expected credit loss methodologies, stress testing, or other relevant prudential and accounting frameworks. Strong data literacy and familiarity with SQL, Python, or similar tools used to analyze portfolio, exposure, and loss trends. Experience working in a regulated payments fintech, digital bank, or financial institution with multiple licenses and banking partnerships. Comfort operating in a high-growth environment with evolving priorities and a bias for practical, scalable execution. title: Head of Data & Intelligence
description: Creandum's edge has always been people: the network, the judgment, the hustle. To sharpen our edge, we need to make everything those people learn compound: every meeting, every diligence process, every founder relationship feeding a shared foundation instead of evaporating into inboxes and individual heads. You will build and own that foundation: the firm's data platform, the intelligence layer on top of it, and the governance that makes partners willing to trust it with their most sensitive work. This is a new function, and you are its first hire. You'll start hands-on-keyboard and stay that way for the time being; but you're building an estate the firm will run on, and the mandate grows with what you prove. You report to the Operating Partner, but work directly and independently with every member of the firm. We believe different viewpoints drive our growth, and we welcome applicants from all backgrounds. What you'll own The data platform. The firm's data architecture end to end: warehouse, ingestion from core systems (CRM, meeting transcripts, documents, email/calendar), entity resolution, and data quality. One person, one company, one deal – consistent across every source. This is foundational; everything else flows from it. The intelligence layer. Retrieval, search & agent tooling that give everyone's AI real firm context, serving both individual workflows (bottom-up) and firm-wide platforms (top-down). Built for passive compounding: the system gets better as people work and as models improve, without depending on anyone's discipline. Access, trust, and AI risk. The access model as structural enforcement, not instructions: who sees what, with identity, provenance, and audit. Sensitive fund and partner data protected to a standard the partnership will trust, plus the AI-specific risk judgment (injection containment, egress, tool guardrails) for everything the function ships, in collaboration with legal/regulatory counsel. Technology strategy and the tool estate. Accountability for whether the firm's tools are the right ones: evaluation, integration, and replacement of the systems and data sources the firm runs on, in close partnership with the stakeholders who use them. Buy when buying is better; build when building is better. You have the mandate to choose, and then execute on your decision. Make sure security, compliance and budget are part of the equation. What you'll deliver First 6 months. A complete map of the firm's data and systems. The foundational data platform stood up. Two or three lightweight tools shipped that visibly improve how a team works. A clear, prioritized 12–18 month roadmap, authored by you and agreed with the partnership. By 12 months. V1 of the firm's shared intelligence layer live and in daily use. The diligence process made genuinely multiplayer; firm knowledge and meeting history informing live deals instead of sitting unused. Measurable adoption, reported honestly, with failures killed as quickly as the wins are shipped. Beyond. The roadmap is yours to define. Candidates for the frontier: productizing how the firm wins deals, network intelligence that answers "who do we know" in seconds, platform tools founders can self-serve, and operational automation across finance, events, and admin. How you'll work Builder first. You ship personally. This is not a role for someone who wants a team of ten doing the building. Co-creation, not solo genius. Stakeholders across the firm (investment, platform, marketing, operations, etc.) steer, test, and tune what you build. Within a year, everyone at the firm should be able to point at something they had a hand in shaping. Product discipline. Prototype, validate with real users, kill what doesn't get adopted. Usage is the metric; expect and budget for churn. Scale deliberately. You start solo. As the foundation proves out, you'll orchestrate internal or external build resources and potentially grow the function. You are prepared to identify, leverage and lead exceptional talent to help achieve results. Who you are You've shipped a real data or AI product end to end (pipelines, retrieval, and the product surface) and people actually used it. Deep, hands-on command of data architecture, warehousing, and governance. Fluent with embeddings, retrieval, and agents that act, not just answer. You treat access control and provenance as product features, not compliance chores. Low ego, high agency, energized by a blank page. Excited to tackle the unglamorous work (entity resolution, data hygiene, permissions) that everything depends on. You can sit with an investor, an EA, and a founder in the same week and design for all of them. Venture experience isn't required, but you'll need to earn a front-line view of the work fast. You can say "no" and "not yet" to smart, senior people and make them glad you did. What this role is not Not IT operations: endpoint, device & office infrastructure are handled by our managed IT partner. Your customers and colleagues find your energy contagious You truly enjoy helping others move and improve. You love helping your customers scale and grow You love goals and objectives. Being able to think and do things at scale is a huge plus You are a trustworthy person who always ensures that deadlines are reached, promises are kept, and you do what is expected of you You are empathetic. You have a strong ability to feel how others are doing. You are also able to communicate in a very empathetic way and touch people's emotions You are fluent in English Why is this role a good fit for you This role is a good fit for you if: You enjoy building long-term relationships with high-touch, Mid Market customers and taking ownership of their success from adoption through expansion. You thrive in a fast-paced, high-volume environment and feel energised by balancing customer conversations, internal collaboration, and proactive problem-solving. You’re motivated by impact and outcomes — helping customers grow, spotting expansion opportunities, and turning feedback into meaningful product improvements excites you. This role is not a good fit for you if: You’re not motivated by customer-facing work or influencing customer outcomes through proactive engagement and collaboration. You’re uncomfortable with project management or coordinating multiple initiatives at the same time. You’re not motivated by upselling, cross-selling, or optimising the long-term value of your customers’ accounts. How you’ll develop in this role In your first 6 months at Pleo, you’ll: Lead customer adoption projects to drive impact in helping high-touch, Mid Market clients maximise the value of Pleo’s solutions. Collaborate with Customer Success and Product teams to improve customer experience processes and feedback loops. Grow your skills in relationship management and upselling strategies, taking on new challenges as the company continues to scale. We’re committed to helping you develop your career, whether that means taking on bigger projects, stepping into leadership, or acquiring new skills in customer success. As these systems become more capable, we need to understand how they could be misused or compromised, which protections matter most, and how to establish that those protections work together.</p> <p>We're hiring an experienced security practitioner to lead this work at the boundary between AI safety and security. You will investigate real systems, develop threat models, test important assumptions and recommend the protections needed for particular capabilities and deployments. Your work will address both dangerous misuse and the protection of sensitive models, data and research.</p> <p>This is an opportunity to help shape a developing area of AI safety through security practice. You will combine technical investigation with careful analysis and clear writing, working closely with our established Security team, researchers and engineers to turn findings into implemented improvements.</p> <p>You will bring security depth and develop your understanding of model capabilities, evaluations and safeguards through that work. Prior experience in AI safety is welcome, but not required.</p> <p><strong>What You'll Be Building</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Threat-model consequential systems and capabilities.</strong> Investigate how dangerous misuse or compromise could occur across models, deployed services and scientific workflows. Identify the relevant actors, access routes and failure paths, and the protections that could interrupt them.</li> <li><strong>Test the assumptions behind our defenses.</strong> Examine architectures, code, configurations and operational evidence. Run focused adversarial tests, build prototypes and investigate weaknesses, including situations where several protections depend on the same underlying system.</li> <li><strong>Shape the protections needed for safe deployment.</strong> Turn dangerous-capability assessments into concrete security requirements. Assess how compromise of models, sensitive assets or supporting systems changes the safety assessment, drawing on personnel, physical and other security specialists where relevant.</li> <li><strong>Make evidence-based recommendations.</strong> Define what evidence would demonstrate that important controls and safeguards work together. Combine findings from model evaluations and security testing, explain the remaining uncertainty, and recommend improvements or conditions for use.</li> <li><strong>Carry findings through to practical improvements.</strong> Work with Security, Safety and engineering owners to prioritize changes, specify acceptance criteria and verify the results. Make clear recommendations about which gaps require attention first and why.</li> <li><strong>Anticipate what more capable systems will require.</strong> Identify where changes in capability, access or deployment call for stronger protections. Help teams plan security work with long lead times, and update assessments as systems change or new evidence emerges.</li> <li><strong>Develop methods that others can use.</strong> Turn your investigations into clear threat models, assessment methods and technical guidance. Help Safety and Security colleagues apply the approach to new problems and build a shared understanding of the evidence behind decisions.</li> </ul> <p><strong>What You'll Need to Succeed</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Substantial hands-on security experience and deep expertise in at least one relevant discipline</strong>, such as security architecture, application or infrastructure security, offensive security, or incident response. You can reason across disciplines and identify when specialist judgment is needed.</li> <li><strong>A record of resolving consequential security problems.</strong> You have investigated ambiguous risks, challenged designs and followed improvements through to validation, including work involving several teams.</li> <li><strong>Strong technical judgment.</strong> You can examine unfamiliar systems, scrutinize code and configurations where relevant, and use technical investigation or testing to distinguish plausible claims from demonstrated protection.</li> <li><strong>Curiosity about AI safety and scientific systems.</strong> You want to understand how model capabilities and safeguards are evaluated, can learn unfamiliar domains quickly, and reason carefully when evidence is incomplete.</li> <li><strong>Clear writing and effective collaboration.</strong> You can explain a technical argument precisely, work through disagreements with specialists and turn a complex investigation into an actionable recommendation.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Bonus Points For</strong></p> <ul> <li>Securing ML infrastructure, model assets, research environments or AI agents.</li> <li>Evaluating safeguards, adversarial robustness or defenses against sophisticated threats.</li> <li>Translating risk assessments into technical requirements, assurance evidence or deployment decisions.</li> <li>Working in scientific or other environments where digital access can have significant real-world consequences.</li> </ul> <p>We value demonstrated security depth, sound judgment and the ability to learn. A research PhD or experience in every security discipline is not required.</p> <p>Your early work will help establish how Lila combines safety and security evidence to make concrete decisions about its systems.</p><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><strong>Compensation</strong></p> <p>We offer competitive base compensation with bonus potential and generous early-stage equity. Your final offer will reflect your background, expertise, and expected impact.</p> <p><strong>U.S. Benefits.</strong> Full-time U.S. employees receive a comprehensive benefits program including medical, dental, and vision coverage; employer-paid life and disability insurance; flexible time off with generous company wide holidays; paid parental leave; an educational assistance program; commuter benefits, including bike share memberships for office based employees; and a company subsidized lunch program.</p> <p><strong>International Benefits.</strong> Full-time employees outside the U.S. receive a comprehensive benefits program tailored to their region. Learn more at www.lila.ai.</p> <p>Guided by our core values of truth, trust, curiosity, grit, and velocity, we move with startup speed while tackling problems of historic importance. You know how to drive an agent, verify its output, and ramp on an unfamiliar codebase with an agent helping you.</p> <p> </p> <h3>What are the responsiblities of the role? </h3> <ul> <li>Design, develop and deliver high-quality web applications and back-end services with modern frameworks and technologies.</li> <li>Work as a part of a high functioning team consisting of UX designers, software ensure the quality of your code.</li> <li>Work with CI/CD tools to ensure that all software developed adheres to both quality and scaling requirements.</li> <li>Take a role in continuously improving repository tools, such as GitLab and GitHub.</li> <li>Experience with productivity tools, such as Jira and Confluence.</li> <li>A good understanding of Agile practices.</li> <li>Ability to accurately
